title: Two qubits & entanglement
source: Lecture Slides - 1 to 7.pdf, PDF pages 29–47; Practice Problems Q11–25.
objectives: Expand tensor products in a fixed basis order.
Test pure two-qubit states for separability.
Prepare and measure a Bell state in Qiskit.
body:
Two systems, one state

We use basis order |00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩, |11⟩. A two-qubit pure state is a|00⟩ + b|01⟩ + c|10⟩ + d|11⟩. Product states factor into two single-qubit vectors. For a nonzero normalized pure state, factorization is possible exactly when ad − bc = 0.

Build a Bell state

Begin at |00⟩. Apply H to the left qubit, giving (|00⟩+|10⟩)/√2. A CNOT controlled by that qubit gives (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2. Here ad−bc=1/2, so the state is entangled.

Each individual bit is random in computational-basis measurement, but their outcomes always agree. Correlations in one measurement basis alone are not proof of entanglement: a classical mixture of 00 and 11 has those correlations too.

Watch the wire order

Qiskit displays q₀ at the top, but a two-qubit ket is written |q₁q₀⟩. To implement the left-qubit Bell construction above, use h(1), then cx(1, 0).

Partial measurement

Project onto the observed outcome and divide surviving amplitudes by the square root of its probability. For a Bell state, observing left bit 0 leaves |00⟩ and observing 1 leaves |11⟩. A zero-probability outcome has no conditional state.

quiz.question: For a normalized pure state with coefficients a,b,c,d, when is it separable?
quiz.explanation: The 2×2 coefficient matrix has rank one exactly when its determinant ad−bc vanishes. This criterion applies to pure two-qubit states.

exercise: Solve Q15, Q16, Q20 and Q25. Then compare Bell-state measurements in Z and X bases in the notebook.
solution: Q16: P(left=0)=1/2 and P(left=1)=1/2. Conditional full states are (|00⟩+|01⟩)/√2 and |11⟩. Q25: q₀=1, q₁=0 means |01⟩.
